sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "in every place where I cause My name to be mentioned" refers literally to the Temple, but the Sages' homiletic interpretation applies it to Torah study, and the drawing down of Ein Sof beyond order through prayer precedes and enables the drawing down through Torah.

translations.translation: And to add,
that the interpretation that "in every place where I cause My name to be mentioned" refers to the Holy Temple, where permission is given to mention the explicit name,
is the simple meaning of the verse
(the Written Torah),
and the interpretation that "I will cause My name to be mentioned" refers to the study of Torah is according to the homiletic exposition of our Sages
(the Oral Torah).
And according to the known principle
that all matters of the Oral Torah are drawn from the Written Torah,
it must be said,

that this—that the teaching that even one who sits and occupies himself with Torah, the Divine Presence rests upon him, is derived from the verse "in every place where I cause My name to be mentioned," which in its simple sense refers to the Temple, which pertains to the matter of service—
is,
because the essential matter of the indwelling of the Divine Presence in the manner of "I will come to you,"
the drawing down of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent
("I will come,"
I Myself),
is through the line of service,
an elevation from below to above.
And as explained in Tanya
that the reason that through prayer Ein Sof above the chain of descent is drawn down
[for through this drawing down a change is effected in the created beings,
to heal the sick and bless the years]
is because of the great superiority of the elevation of mayin nukvin.
And through prayer, this drawing down subsequently comes also into Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section emphasizes that the drawing down of Ein Sof beyond order through prayer and Torah is primarily through communal prayer and communal Torah study, where the drawing down is disproportionate to the arousal from below.

translations.translation: And according to what is stated in the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah
(cited above in section 1)
that this—that through prayer and through Torah one draws down the revelation of the light of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent—is primarily in communal prayer
and in communal Torah,
to the extent that the drawing down through communal prayer and communal Torah is disproportionate to the arousal from below
(of the many),
it is understood,
that the aforementioned matter—that the drawing down of that which is above the chain of descent in Torah is through prayer—
is even more pronounced in the drawing down through the many.
And as explained above
(in the maamar of Yud-Gimmel Tammuz),
that the reason that the matter of the drawing down disproportionate to the elevation through communal Torah is learned
(in the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah)
from the drawing down through communal prayer,
is,
because the essence and source of this matter is in prayer,
and through this it is subsequently drawn also into Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the essential drawing down of Ein Sof beyond order is specifically through the elevation of mayin nukvin in prayer, because prayer involves true self-nullification, whereas Torah study, even with great effort, involves comprehension and is not true nullification.

translations.translation: And although the superiority of the elevation of mayin nukvin seemingly exists also in Torah,
as explained in the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah
that also in Torah there must be service and effort,
nevertheless,
the essential matter of the drawing down of that which is above the chain of descent is specifically through the elevation of mayin nukvin of prayer.
And the point of the explanation in this is,
that the superiority of the service of man
(the elevation of mayin nukvin)
through which Ein Sof above the chain of descent is drawn down,
is
(primarily)
when the service is in a state of self-nullification,
and the matter of self-nullification is in the service of prayer.
For the effort in the study of Torah,
since the matter of study is that one should understand and comprehend what he learns,
therefore the effort in Torah,
even the effort of one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times,
even though this effort is not
(only)
for the sake of understanding the Torah but rather in order to change his nature and habit,
is not truly the matter of self-nullification,
because even the study of the one hundred and first time is with understanding and comprehension.
And the essential self-nullification is in the service of prayer,
for the person who prays is like a servant
before his Master.
And it may be said,
that even the service of prayer that is for the sake of the occupation with Torah
(for "anyone who says I have nothing but Torah, even Torah he does not have"),
since the prayer is for the sake of Torah, whose matter is understanding and comprehension,
is not truly the matter of self-nullification.
Therefore the essential matter of the drawing down of that which is above the chain of descent
(and all the more so a drawing down disproportionate to the elevation)
is through the elevation of mayin nukvin of prayer,
and through this it is subsequently drawn also into Torah.
For through the service in Torah
[the service of prayer that is for the sake of Torah,
and below that—the service of one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times in order to change his nature and habit,
and below that—the effort in understanding the Torah],
the Torah that he studies is a vessel for the drawing down of that which is above the chain of descent that comes through prayer.
